agency_name: Colorado Parks and Wildlife
notes: CO legislature established Dept of Game and Fish Apr 27 1899. First licenses administered in 1903 under Commissioner Woodard. ~185 GMUs with both sequential and 3-digit sub-unit numbers. Big game licenses allotted per GMU via OTC or limited draw with preference points.

agency_name: Georgia Department of Natural Resources Wildlife Resources Division
notes: GA Dept of Game and Fish established 1911 financed by license fees. Self-sustaining from inception. 148 wardens by 1913. 104 WMAs exist but licensing is statewide; either-sex days and bag limits set by county. Big Game License required as add-on for deer/turkey/bear.

agency_name: Illinois Department of Natural Resources
notes: IL hunting license law enacted 1903. First license issued Jun 11 1903 in Sangamon County to Horace S. Rearden. 12000 licenses issued statewide in Jul 1903. Firearm deer permits county-specific lottery. FOID card required for all firearms hunting.

agency_name: Indiana Department of Natural Resources
notes: Earliest known IN hunting license is 1901 Indiana Hunter's License (collector records). Lifetime licenses discontinued Jul 1 2005; existing ones honored. Antlerless bag limits set per county. Waterfowl managed by 3 zones (North/Central/South).

agency_name: Iowa Department of Natural Resources
notes: Earliest known IA hunting license is 1909 Resident Hunting License (collector records). Mandatory Habitat Fee required for all hunters. Deer tags county-specific with quotas. Low-income seniors 65+ and permanently disabled get free licenses.

agency_name: Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks
agency_name_historical: Kansas Forestry Fish and Game Commission
notes: Earliest known KS hunting license is 1905-06 Resident License to Hunt (collector records). 105 counties; 21 DMUs (groups of counties) for big game permits. Units 8A and 10A are military installations. Base hunting license is statewide; big game permits are DMU-specific.

agency_name: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
notes: KY Game and Fish Commission formed by legislature in 1912; generated $31000 from license sales in first 5 months. County licenses eliminated 1952; only statewide licenses since. License year Mar 1-Feb 28. Children under 12 exempt. Farmland owners exempt on own land (except deer/turkey).

agency_name: Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife
agency_name_historical: Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife
notes: Earliest known ME license is 1903 NR Hunting License (collector records). WMDs created ~2000 (originally 30 reduced to 29 in 2006). Pre-2000 antique licenses would not reference WMDs. Super Pack license is all-inclusive. Alien (non-US citizen) NR category exists.

agency_name: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
notes: MD 1872 law required $20 license for sink-box waterfowl hunting on Susquehanna Flats — earliest known US hunting license of any kind. General county hunting licenses ~1910 (earliest known specimen: 1910 Baltimore County NR license). Statewide licenses ~1916-18. 23 counties + Baltimore City = 24 jurisdictions.

agency_name: Michigan Department of Natural Resources
notes: Michigan among first states to require hunting license in 1895 (resident $0.50/NR $25) specifically for deer. 83 counties; many Lower Peninsula DMUs correspond to single counties. DMU numbering non-contiguous (001-486+).

agency_name: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources
notes: MN first required resident hunting license in 1899 at $0.25 (NR $25). Species-specific license system (no single general hunting license). 87 counties; DPAs group counties by habitat/land use. Hunters must declare DPA at deer license purchase.

agency_name: Missouri Department of Conservation
notes: MO uses 'permits' not 'licenses' for hunting credentials. Earliest known MO hunting license Jan 6 1913 (county resident hunter's license). MO Conservation Commission formed 1937. Residents 65+ exempt from small game/bird permits. Antlerless deer quotas set by county. 114 counties + St. Louis City.

agency_name: Montana Fish Wildlife and Parks
notes: NR hunting license required 1901; resident license required 1905. Fish and Game Board established 1895. ~300+ Hunting Districts statewide; district count varies by species. Conservation License + Base Hunting License required before any species license.

agency_name: New Hampshire Fish and Game Department
agency_name_historical: New Hampshire Fish and Game Department
notes: Earliest known NH license is 1909 Resident Hunter's Permit (collector records). NH Fish & Game created 1906. 13 main WMU letters (A-M) with 22 subunits. Units L and M are special deer management units. Senior threshold is 68+. Permanent/Milestone licenses free for those born 1947 or earlier.

agency_name: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
notes: Earliest known NY hunting license is 1908 Resident Hunter's License (collector records). 1864 date references earliest game law. WMUs replaced DMUs after 1997-98 season. WMU numbers correspond to DEC Regions (1-9). Deer Management Permits (antlerless) issued by WMU quota. Seniors 70+ hunt free.

agency_name: North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission
notes: NC General Statutes cite 1935 c.486 as earliest hunting license session law. Earlier game regulation laws from 1929 existed. NC Wildlife Resources Commission formally created 1947. Reciprocal 10-day rates with GA/SC/TN/VA. Comprehensive license adds big game + waterfowl to base hunting license.

agency_name: Ohio Department of Natural Resources Division of Wildlife
agency_name_historical: Ohio Department of Natural Resources Division of Wildlife
notes: OH was one of five states issuing first resident hunting licenses in 1913. Earliest known OH license issued Sep 27 1913. Multi-year licenses (3/5/10-year) available for residents. Free senior license for those born on/before Dec 31 1937.

agency_name: Pennsylvania Game Commission
notes: First PA hunting license sold in 1913 for $1. PA Game Commission created 1895 but licenses not required until 1913. Pre-2003 licenses county-based; 22 WMUs replaced counties as management overlay in 2003. Antlerless deer quotas were by county 1951-2002. County remains the primary unit on historical antique licenses.

agency_name: Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency
notes: Earliest known TN hunting license is 1920 county license to hunt (collector records). Actual statutory requirement may be earlier. TWRA established 1974. TN uses supplemental licenses on top of base Combo Hunt/Fish. NR Native Tennessean (born in TN) gets resident rates.

agency_name: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department
agency_name_historical: Office of Game Fish and Oyster Commissioner
notes: Texas State Historical Association confirms first hunting licenses sold in 1909. Office of Game Fish and Oyster Commissioner established 1907. Regulations set by county in the Outdoor Annual.

agency_name: Vermont Fish and Wildlife Department
notes: VT Fish & Wildlife official presentation states 1908 first resident hunting and fishing license. Some sources say 1909. Fish & Game Dept created 1906. WMUs established 1979; pre-1979 antique licenses unlikely to reference management units. 17 base letter units with D/E/F/J subdivided into numbered subunits.

agency_name: Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources
agency_name_historical: Department of Game and Inland Fisheries
notes: Earliest known VA hunting license is 1916-17 county hunter's license (collector records). VA uniquely offers county/city-specific resident hunting license cheaper than statewide. Multi-year licenses available up to 4 years. 95 counties + 38 independent cities = 133 jurisdictions.

agency_name: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources
agency_name_historical: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources
notes: WV first NR hunting license 1899 ($25). First resident license 1909-10. Game and Fish Warden office created 1897. WV uses Class code system (A/E/X/BG/CS etc.) for all license types. Antlerless deer stamps (Class N/NN) are county-specific. Conservation Stamp required for all hunters.

agency_name: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources
notes: First WI hunting license 1897: $1 resident/$30 nonresident. ~12000 licenses sold first year. First deer license to George Ogomoso of Armstrong Creek. ~130 DMUs currently used for deer management; county remains the historical unit for antique licenses.

agency_name: Wyoming Game and Fish Department
notes: Game Warden office created 1899; fishing license not required until 1920. Hunting license start year unconfirmed — estimated 1899-1905. Hunt Areas vary by species; deer ~90 areas elk ~100+ antelope ~100+. Conservation Stamp required for all hunters.

agency_name: New Jersey Division of Fish and Wildlife
notes: NJDEP states the first NJ license was a nonresident hunting license in 1902 at $10.50; the first resident hunting license was required in 1909 at $1.15; first fishing license 1915. Earliest known specimen is a 1909 NJ Resident Hunter's License (collector records). Licenses run the calendar year and by law must be openly displayed in the middle of the back on outer clothing - a direct back-tag practice. Base licenses are statewide; deer, bear and turkey permits are Deer Management Zone specific. 21 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Delaware Division of Fish and Wildlife
notes: DE was one of five states to issue its first resident hunting license in 1913 (with AZ, AR, OH and PA). Earliest known specimen is the 1913 Delaware Resident Hunter's License. License year runs July 1 - June 30. Only 3 counties (New Castle, Kent, Sussex), making DE the smallest county set in the dataset. Hunter education required for those born after Jan 1 1967; trapper education for those born after Jan 1 1978. Conservation Access Pass required for vehicles using state wildlife areas. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Massachusetts Division of Fisheries and Wildlife
notes: Earliest known MA hunting credential is the 1909 Resident Hunter's Certificate (collector records); the 1780 MA fishing license is a fishing document, not hunting. Agency founded 1866 as a state fisheries commission, game added to its authority 1886, Commissioners on Fisheries and Game from 1902, replaced Dec 1 1919 by the Division of Fisheries and Game, renamed Division of Fisheries and Wildlife in 1974. Licenses have long been sold through city and town clerks, which is the true historical point of issue. Modern management is by 15 Wildlife Management Zones; counties are listed here as the durable geographic unit. 14 counties.

agency_name: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection Wildlife Division
notes: Earliest known CT hunting license is the 1907-08 Resident License to Hunt (collector records). Licenses and stamps are sold through DEEP, most town clerks and outdoor retailers; town clerk issuance is the historical point of sale. Licenses run the calendar year. Deer permits are split by land type (state land lottery, state land no-lottery, private land) and by weapon rather than by county. CT counties were retained only as geographic areas and the Census adopted 9 planning regions as county equivalents in 2022; the 8 legacy counties are listed here as the durable historical unit. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management Division of Fish and Wildlife
notes: Earliest known RI hunting license is the 1916 Resident Hunter's Certificate (collector records); the 1807 RI cod fishing license is a commercial fishing document, not hunting. License year runs March 1 through the last day of February. Licenses are sold at the DEM Providence licensing office, most city and town clerks and sporting goods stores. Deer permits are antler, weapon and zone specific and one permit is required per animal harvested. Only 5 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources
notes: Earliest known SC hunting licenses are 1916-17 county licenses from Horry and Richland Counties (collector records), confirming county-based issuance from the outset. The modern base license is statewide with a separate Big Game Permit required for bear, deer and turkey. Four Game Zones set season structure; bear tags are Game Zone 1 (Mountains) only. Hunter education required for anyone born after June 30 1979. 46 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources Division of Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries
notes: Earliest known AL hunting license is the 1917 Alabama County Hunter's License (collector records), confirming county-based issuance. ADCNR was formed in 1971, succeeding the Alabama Department of Conservation. License year ends August 31. Licenses are issued through county Probate Offices and License Commissioners as well as agents and online, so the county remains the point of issue. Residents 65 and over are exempt from hunting, WMA and state duck stamp fees; optional 65-plus licenses exist for those who wish to contribute. 67 counties.

agency_name: Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks
notes: Earliest known MS hunting license is the 1926-27 Mississippi County Hunting License (collector records); the actual statutory requirement may be earlier and the 1926 floor should be treated as a specimen floor rather than a first-year. Licenses are sold at county circuit clerk offices as well as agents and online. All deer, turkey and hog hunters must hold either an All Game Hunting/Fishing or a Sportsman's License. 82 counties, the largest county set among the ten states added in this pass. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
notes: Earliest known FL hunting license is the 1917-18 Florida Nonresident County Hunter's License (collector records); a resident county license very likely ran alongside it but no specimen is recorded in this source. Licenses are sold through county tax collectors' offices as well as agents and Go Outdoors Florida, so the county remains the point of issue. The license exemption applies to persons hunting in their county of residence on their own homestead, which keeps county on the face of the regulation. 67 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission
notes: AR was one of five states to issue its first resident hunting license in 1913 (with AZ, DE, OH and PA); the earliest known specimen is a 1913 Arkansas County Hunting License, confirming county-based issuance in the first year. License year ends June 30. AGFC prints short product codes on licenses (CS, RS, HNT, NBG, AG3, DSR and similar) which are useful identifiers on modern issues. Deer, turkey and bear tags are bundled with the base Sportsman's License rather than sold separately. 75 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Alaska Department of Fish and Game
notes: FLOOR UNVERIFIED. The earliest Alaska items recorded in the collector gallery are a 1922 Territory of Alaska Nonresident Fisherman's License and a 1927-28 Alaska Resident Trapping License - neither is a hunting license, so the hunting floor is genuinely unknown and 1922 should be read as an any-license floor only. Alaska's real hunting geography is its 26 numbered Game Management Units, not boroughs; GMUs appear on harvest tickets and permits. Boroughs and census areas are listed here as the Census county-equivalents. Structure: hunting licence, free harvest tickets for general-season big game, species locking-tags (required of nonresidents and of residents for brown/grizzly bear and muskox), plus drawing, registration and Tier I/II subsistence permits. 30 county-equivalents; Valdez-Cordova was abolished 2 Jan 2019 and split into Chugach and Copper River.

agency_name: Arizona Game and Fish Department
notes: AZ was one of five states to issue its first resident hunting license in 1913 (with AR, DE, OH and PA); earliest known specimen is a 1913 Arizona Hunting License. Licenses run 365 days from purchase. There is no standalone nonresident hunting-only license - nonresidents buy the Combination Hunt and Fish. Big game requires a hunt permit-tag, mostly allocated through three annual draw cycles; fall bear, archery turkey, archery deer and mountain lion are non-permit tags. AZGFD is funded by licence and tag revenue rather than the state general fund. Only 15 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: California Department of Fish and Wildlife
notes: Earliest known CA hunting licenses are the Type I and Type II 1907-08 California Hunting Licenses, issued as metal badges rather than paper - a distinctive and highly collectible form. California contracted J.M. Patrick of San Francisco to produce its first licenses, and later chromolithographed pictorial licenses (Mysell-Rollins 1914-15, Schwabacher-Frey 1923-24) are believed to have inspired the first federal waterfowl stamp. License year runs July 1 - June 30. CA uses validations rather than stamps (Upland Game Bird, California Duck, Wild Pig) and a lettered deer zone system (A, B, C, D, X) with general, restricted and premium tag categories. 58 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Hawaii Department of Land and Natural Resources Division of Forestry and Wildlife
notes: Earliest known HI hunting credentials are 1911-12 County of Hawaii, County of Honolulu and County of Maui Hunting Permits, plus a 1921-22 County of Kauai Hunting License - Hawaii issued at the county level from the outset, and the county name is printed on the artifact. Note these are Territory-era documents; Hawaii did not become a state until 1959. 5 counties, including Kalawao, the smallest county in the US, administered by the Department of Health. Modern license products not researched in this pass.

agency_name: Idaho Department of Fish and Game
notes: Earliest known ID credential is the 1906 Idaho Fish and Game License (collector records). Calendar-year licenses. The Resident Sportsman's Package bundles a combination license with deer, elk, bear, mountain lion, wolf, turkey, salmon and steelhead tags, with archery and muzzleloader validated on the license itself. A Depredation Management/Access fee is applied to all annual hunting, fishing and trapping licenses. Idaho runs a Price Lock discount for residents with continuous purchase history. 44 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries
notes: Earliest known LA credential is the 1908 Louisiana License to Hunt (collector records). LOUISIANA USES PARISHES, NOT COUNTIES - 64 parishes, the only state in the dataset with this unit type. Structure is a Basic Hunting License plus stacked special licenses (Deer, Turkey, Waterfowl) and a WMA Access Permit; the Sportsman's Paradise License bundles all of them with fishing. Residents 60 and over must instead hold a Senior Hunting/Fishing License, free for those born before June 1 1940. Nonresidents born in Louisiana may buy Nonresident Native licenses valid ten consecutive days. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Nebraska Game and Parks Commission
notes: Earliest known NE credential is the 1901 Nebraska License to Hunt and Fish (collector records); a sheet-type 1913 Nebraska License to Fish and Hunt is also recorded. 93 counties. Modern license products not researched in this pass. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Nevada Department of Wildlife
notes: Earliest known NV credentials are 1909-10 licenses including a Nonresident Hunting License, a Duplicate Hunting License and county-issued examples from Lyon County and (probably) White Pine County - so Nevada issued at county level in this era and the county name appears on the artifact. 16 counties plus Carson City, a consolidated municipality independent of any county. Modern license products not researched in this pass. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: New Mexico Department of Game and Fish
notes: Earliest known NM credentials are the 1909 Territory of New Mexico Bird Hunting License and 1909 Territory of New Mexico General Hunting License, followed by 1912 State of New Mexico licenses. The territorial-to-state transition in 1912 is printed on the documents and is a meaningful collecting distinction: pre-1912 items read 'Territory of New Mexico'. 33 counties. Modern license products not researched in this pass. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: North Dakota Game and Fish Department
notes: Earliest known ND credential is the 1898 North Dakota Resident Hunting Permit (collector records) - among the earliest resident hunting documents recorded for any state, predating all but Michigan (1895), Wisconsin (1897) and a handful of others. 53 counties. Modern license products not researched in this pass. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Oklahoma Department of Wildlife Conservation
notes: Earliest known OK credential is the 1909-10 Oklahoma Resident License to Hunt (collector records), issued only two years after statehood in 1907. Structure is an annual hunting license plus separate species licenses for deer, elk, antelope, bear and turkey, an Oklahoma waterfowl license, HIP permit and a land access permit for designated areas. The lifetime hunting license was discontinued as of July 1 2024, which fixes a hard end date on that product. 77 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife
notes: Earliest known OR credentials are 1905 county hunter's licenses from Jackson, Marion and Wasco Counties - Oregon issued at county level in this era and the county name appears on the artifact. Structure is an annual hunting license plus species tags and validations; the Sports Pac bundles hunting, angling and shellfish licenses with deer, elk, bear and cougar tags and the upland bird validation. Oregon has distinctive senior categories: a Senior license at 70 with 5 years residency, and a Pioneer Combination at 65 with 50 years residency. 36 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks
notes: Earliest known SD credential is a 1903 South Dakota Hunter's License, with a recorded Deadwood example (collector records). 66 counties - note Shannon County was renamed Oglala Lakota County in 2015 and its FIPS code changed from 46113 to 46102, so pre-2015 artifacts will read Shannon. Modern license products not researched in this pass. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Utah Division of Wildlife Resources
notes: Earliest known UT credential is the 1908 Utah Permit to Hunt and Fish (collector records). Utah draws a hard distinction between licenses and permits: a hunting license or combination license is required first, and species hunts need a separate permit obtained over the counter or through a draw. Licenses are valid 365 days from purchase, with multiyear options. Deer and elk permits are split into general-season (preference points) and limited-entry (50/50 points and random) tiers. 29 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.

agency_name: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
notes: Earliest known WA hunting credentials are the 1901-02 Pierce County and 1901 Whatcom County Hunter's Licenses - Washington issued at county level in this era and the county name appears on the artifact. Earlier 1899-1900 Washington items are commercial fishing licenses, not hunting. License year runs April 1 - March 31. WDFW sells big game as bundled species packages rather than standalone tags, and issues transport tags plus a Migratory Bird Authorization and Harvest Record Card. 39 counties. Historical agency name not verified in this pass.
